tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear Path for Target Disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a target disk that is not on top, relocate every smaller disk that sits above it to other pegs so the target becomes the topmost disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a disk that has one or more smaller disks stacked on top of it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If disk 4 is under disk 2 on a peg, first move disk 2 elsewhere, then move disk 4.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Build Goal Stack in Decreasing Size
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Construct the final tower on the goal peg by placing disks from the largest down to the smallest, each new disk resting directly on the immediate larger one already there.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When assembling the final configuration on the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After disk 5 is at the bottom of peg 2, place disk 4, then disk 3, then disk 2, then disk 1.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Phase Planning (Move‑k‑Disks)
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a stack of k disks, recursively move the top k‑1 disks to an auxiliary peg, move the k‑th (largest) disk to the target peg, then move the k‑1 disks onto it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to transfer a contiguous stack of disks between pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move disks 3, 2, 1 from peg A to peg B, first move 2 and 1 to peg C, then move 3 to B, then move 2 and 1 onto 3.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Do Not Prematurely Place Small Disks on Goal
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never leave a small disk on the goal peg while any larger disk that must sit below it has not yet been placed there; temporary placements must be moved away before larger disks are added.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When considering moving a small disk onto the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Do not keep disk 1 on the goal peg while disk 4 is still missing; move disk 1 elsewhere first.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Legal Move Invariant
tower-of-hanoi.principle: A move is legal only if the source disk is the topmost on its peg and the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: You cannot move disk 3 from a peg if disk 2 is on top of it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat Existing Goal Disks as Fixed Base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Once a disk is correctly placed on the goal peg with all larger disks beneath it also correctly placed, treat it as immovable for the remainder of the solution.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After a disk has reached its final position in the goal stack.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After placing disk 5 at the bottom of peg 2, never move it again.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Exploit the Smallest Disk’s Flexibility
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any peg without violating size constraints, making it an ideal temporary buffer for clearing paths or occupying pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need a disposable disk to free a larger one or to hold a peg temporarily.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Move disk 1 to an empty peg to free disk 3 on another peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Post‑Construction Verification
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After generating the full move list, replay the moves from the initial configuration to confirm that every move is legal and that the final configuration matches the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After you have produced a candidate move sequence, before submitting it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Simulate each move step‑by‑step and check that peg 2 ends with the ordered stack [5,4,3,2,1].

tower-of-hanoi.title: Generate Moves Recursively with Explicit Disk IDs
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When implementing the recursive Hanoi algorithm, explicitly name the disk being moved in each step to avoid ambiguity and to produce the required output format.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: While constructing the move list, either programmatically or manually.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Record a move as [3, 0, 2] meaning “move disk 3 from peg 0 to peg 2”.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Move Two Smallest Disks as a Unit
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When a target disk is blocked by exactly two smaller disks, clear the path using a three‑move pattern: move the smallest to the goal, move the second smallest to the auxiliary peg, then move the smallest onto the second smallest.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the top two disks on a peg are the smallest ones and you need to free the third (larger) disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: With disks 1 and 2 atop disk 3 on a peg, move 1 to the goal, 2 to the spare peg, then 1 onto 2, leaving 3 free.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may forget the size ordering rule and treat moves like arbitrary transfers.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always check that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk before committing a move.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempting to move a disk that is not the topmost on its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model can overlook the stack nature of pegs and try to access buried disks.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Verify that the chosen source peg's top disk matches the intended disk ID before moving.

tower-of-hanoi.description: The sequence of moves ends with a configuration that differs from the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may lose track of the overall objective while focusing on local moves.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: After generating the move list, replay it (post‑construction verification) to ensure the final state matches the goal.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Using the wrong peg numbers (e.g., 1 instead of 0) when listing moves.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: Off‑by‑one errors or confusion about 0‑indexing can lead to incorrect peg references.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Keep a clear mapping of peg indices throughout the solution and double‑check each move's source and destination numbers.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Placing a small disk onto the goal peg before all larger required disks have been positioned beneath it.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may prioritize moving the smallest disk because it is most flexible, forgetting the final ordering constraint.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Apply the “Do Not Prematurely Place Small Disks on Goal” principle: only leave a small disk on the goal peg after every larger disk that belongs below it is already placed.
